subject: integer arithmetic in Stan may not do what you expect

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: integer arithmetic in Stan may not do what you expect
parts:
Andrew's been using Stan in his Bayesian Data Analysis
class, and a student brought up this issue:

>> When I am doing Computing problem (b), I used nu ~ exponential(1/10) as a prior and the program cannot work, then I
>> tried nu ~ exponential(0.1) and it works... What is the difference?

We use standard IEEE arithmetic (as in C++ or Java), where
integer divisions like (1/10) round down to 0. If you want floating
point division, you need to write (1.0 / 10.0) instead.

I should probably put something in the model translator
to warn users who try to divide integers by integers, as
that's going to be the main source of problems.

This is in the manual and in the differences from BUGS appendix.
We're trying to not overload the getting-started examples too much.

- Bob
